lines.text: Evening, everybody. Uncle June here, same bench, same mic, under the same cherry trees at Blossom Park. Let's play some ball.
Welcome to Blossom Park and the Spring Invitational. Petals on the court, ice cream on the cart, and Uncle June on the mic.
Now settle in, folks. I've been calling games in this park since half these cherry trees were twigs. Let's see who blooms.
Spring air, pink sky, and the old-timers arguing on the bench. This is Blossom Park, and I'm Uncle June. Pull up a seat.
Bench regulars, let me hear you! Cornbread, I see you with your folding chair.
Ice cream line, you can cheer and wait at the same time!
Left side of the fountain, you're quieter than the petals. Let's fix that.
Checkers table, put the game down for one minute and holler with me!
Sunday crew in the back, I know you can still get loud. Show them!
Birdie brought the whole family again. Family, let this park hear you!
Back in my day, our rim was a bicycle wheel nailed to the old cherry tree. Worked fine.
Rollie's ice cream cart is out. Strawberry's gone already. Pistachio? Plenty of pistachio. Always is.
The old folks used to tell me, you can't hurry spring. Took me sixty years to listen.
Petals on the court again. Don't sweep them, folks. That's not a mess, that's the season.
Hollis still plays every Sunday. Hasn't hit a layup since the lamps went up. Never missed a Sunday.
Cornbread says rain's coming. Cornbread's said that every day for thirty years. Right about twice.
Smell that spring air. Cut grass, cherry blossoms, and whatever's melting on the ice cream cart.
People ask why I've called games here forty years. Simple. Best seat in the park, and it's free.
Getting a little June weather out here.
Well, now. Something's starting to bloom.
Easy, sprout. You're finding something.
Oh, the bench is up now. That's rare.
Tell Rollie to hold the cart. Nobody's leaving.
That's warm. That's real warm, youngster.
Rollie's giving out free cones now!
Hold on, now. Hold on! Can't miss!
Whole park's up! Even the checkers table!
Petals are dancing for this one!
Cold snap. Happens every April. Shake it off.
Frost in the morning, blossoms by noon, sprout.
Rim's being stubborn. Keep knocking, it opens.
Somebody find a ribbon for the old tree. Blossom Park has a new name to remember.
Forty years on this mic, that's near the top. Go get some ice cream, champ.
The bench remembers, youngster. Come back anytime, your seat's got your name on it.
Well, well. You came to Blossom Park a bud and you're leaving in full bloom.
Rain waters the flowers too, youngster. Come on back, the bench will save your spot.
Not today. But I've seen many springs, and the good ones always come back around.
Back in my day, I lost here three summers straight. Then I didn't. Run it back.
That's a good showing, sprout. The petals will be here tomorrow, and so will the rematch.
It's Flight Night under the cherry trees. Two rounds, two dunks apiece, five judges on the bench, and a rival loitering by the ice cream cart.
Flight Night, folks! Two rounds, two dunks each, five judges who've seen it all, and a rival who thinks this park belongs to them.
Now, the dunk contest is the only time I let anybody hang on my rim. Five judges, two rounds, two dunks each. Rival's waiting.
Back again? Good. The petals missed you, and so did the bench.
Another Flight Night. Cart's restocked, lamps are on, and I'm not going anywhere.
Look who came back to Blossom Park. That's how the regulars start, youngster.
Tonight's rival came to my park to take something home. Let's see about that.
Across the way, tonight's other dunker. Give them a polite hand, folks. Just polite.
Cass. Steady as a porch swing. Same tomahawk every time, and it never once misses.
Ty. Doesn't say much. Doesn't need to. That windmill does all the talking, all night.
Pilot. Sits back, reads the whole park, then spins a three-sixty through it. Patient, like me.
Zo. Came for the cameras, and the trophy's an afterthought. Wave, folks. Zo's already posing.
Stack. Starts with the hardest dunk there is and laughs the whole way. Youth.
All right, sprout. Your stage.
Quiet down, bench. Let the youngster work.
Here we go. Show this park something.
Take your time. Spring's not going anywhere.
Petals are falling. Let's see you rise.
Again. Nobody blooms on the first try.
That's fine. Dust it off. One more.
One try, back in my day. Lucky you.
Easy now. Plant your feet and go.
Last one, youngster. Make this spring count.
Third try. Even the checkers game stopped.
Now or never, sprout. Whole park's watching.
Go on, now.
Now then!
Up you go!
Rise, sprout!
Let's see it.
Well, that'll do.
Clean. Sensible. I respect sensible.
All right, all right. Honest work.
Solid. Won't wake the neighbors, but solid.
Plain as Sunday toast, and just as good.
Gets the job done. Old-timers approve.
Now that's pretty. Real pretty.
Ooh, the judges liked that one!
Look at that! Petals went flying!
Whoa! I felt that on the bench!
Somebody tell the checkers table what they missed!
There it is! That's Blossom Park basketball!
Easy, easy... no, go ahead and cheer!
Ring the ice cream bell, Rollie!
Oh, now hold on. Hold on!
Tie a ribbon on the old tree!
Call the Sunday crew! They won't believe me!
Wait. Wait a minute. Wait a minute!
Bench, you seeing this?! You seeing this?!
Rollie dropped the whole ice cream cart!
Get me off this bench! Get me up!
The petals stopped falling! They stopped to watch!
In all my springs... I have never!
Good gracious alive! What did I just see?!
Fifty! Folks, this bench has waited years for that!
Perfect fifty! Five judges agreeing? That never happens here!
Five tens, under my cherry trees. Mercy!
Last fifty I saw out here, the lamps were gas.
I've heard that story before, and so have the judges.
Pretty. Pretty familiar, too.
Seen that bloom already this spring. Plant something new.
The bench remembers that one. Judges do too.
Not this time. That rim's seen it all.
Well. Can't win them all, sprout.
Ooh. That one got away.
Close. Close isn't a bucket, but it's close.
Easy. Even the cherry trees drop a few.
Back in my day, that counted. Not today.
In and out. The rim's being greedy.
Went in for a visit, didn't stay.
Oh, that iron's got a temper tonight.
Lost it in the petals, I suppose.
That lob had other plans.
Never caught it. Ball wanted ice cream.
Caught a piece of it going over.
Oh, you clipped it. Clear it next time.
Over it, sprout. Not through it.
That's three. We'll mark it down and move along, gently.
Out of tries. Judges have to call it a miss.
No more tries on that one. Let it go, sprout.
Judges, your cards.
Let's hear it, judges.
Well, judges?
What say you, judges?
Rival's turn. Show them some spring hospitality.
The visitor's up. Mind your manners, bench.
Cass is up. Same as always, I expect.
Ty's up. Hold on to your ice cream.
Pilot's been watching. Now Pilot moves.
Zo's up. Phones out, apparently.
Stack's up, grinning. Never a good sign.
Credit where it's due, folks.
Can't argue with that one, sprout.
Well, the visitor came ready.
Clean, I'll give them that.
Cass. Porch swing steady, as usual...
Ty put the whole park on notice!
Patient as a gardener, that Pilot...
Zo got the shot for the phones!
Look at that. Stack pulled it off...
Came up empty. Happens under these trees.
Oh, that didn't go to plan.
Missed. Even the visitors get spring fever.
No luck. The rim's a Blossom Park regular.
That's an opening, youngster. Walk right through it.
Round two. The final round. This is where the old-timers lean in.
Final round. In my day, that's when the lamps came on.
Second round, last round. Everything you saved, spend it now.
Trailing, sprout. You'll need something this bench has never seen.
Chasing now. Time to go big or go get ice cream.
Down, but it's still spring. Big numbers, youngster. Big ones.
Out in front. Don't get fancy, just finish the job.
Ahead now. Close it out slow and sure, like locking the gate.
Oh, now hold on! We have a champion! Blossom Park, make some noise!
Champion of Flight Night! Rollie, the ice cream's on the house for this one.
Every champion gets a spot on the bench, sprout. Scoot over, Cornbread.
I'm going to be telling this one on Sundays for years. Flight Night is yours!
The visitor takes Flight Night. Shake hands, sprout, then come back and take it home.
Rival's night. Every champion on that bench lost here first, youngster. Ask Cornbread.
Blossoms fall every spring, and they come right back. So will you, sprout.
Well, that's the contest. Rival earned it. You earned a rematch, and I'll be right here.
The splits! Old dance hall move, that one.
Calling it over already? Bold. Might be right.
A roar! The checkers table jumped!
Too small, is it? Somebody raise the rim!
Arms up! Soak it in. Petals and all.
Hand over the controller, gently now. Next!
Trade places, friends. The other one's up.
Player one, you're up. Show me something.
Your turn, player two. Take the controller.
Settled! Other one's buying the ice cream.
Player one wins it! Save a spot on the bench!
Duel goes to player two! The bench saw it all.
Nobody wins, nobody loses. Guess you'll both come back Sunday.
A tie. The cherry trees won't mind. Run it back.
Welcome to Downtown, Blossom Park style. Six shooters, five racks, sixty seconds. Mind the money balls. Top three move on.
Shooting contest. Set shots in my day, but go on. Five racks, sixty seconds, six shooters. Top three advance.
Now, this one's for the patient ones. Five racks, the money balls, sixty seconds. Six shoot, three advance.
Take your time. Quickly.
Go on, then!
Let it fly!
Next rack, please.
Move along now.
Keep strolling.
Onward, youngster.
Last rack. Finish your plate.
Final rack, youngster. Empty it.
One more rack. Make it sweet.
Money ball. Counts double.
Here's the good one.
Worth two, youngster.
This one pays.
There it is.
Good.
Sweet.
Counts.
Pretty.
That'll do.
Money ball, cashed.
Double, and deserved.
Ooh, that pays nicely.
Ring the bell, Rollie!
Pity.
Didn't drop.
Next one.
Almost.
Nearly.
Like clockwork, folks.
Now we're cooking.
One after another.
Oh, the bench likes this.
My word. Can't miss, can it?
Somebody tell the old-timers!
Whole rack! Not a crumb left!
Pure spring water, every one!
Late frost. It'll pass.
Patience. The rim remembers you.
Slow down, sprout. Old-timer pace.
Ten seconds, youngster!
Step lively, ten seconds!
Last ten, now hurry!
Horn went, ball still counts!
Out before the horn. Counts!
Beat the buzzer! Count it!
Here come the numbers. Shooter by shooter, now.
Let's see the board. Patience, folks, one at a time.
You're moving on, sprout. The final's waiting, and the bench is too.
Through to the final! Blossom Park's got a shooter.
Advancing. Don't celebrate yet, youngster. Save some for the final.
Out in qualifying. That's all right. The rim will be here tomorrow.
Not this time, sprout. Shoot a few hundred and come see me.
Didn't make the cut. Back in my day, neither did I. Twice.
The final, youngster. You've seen the number. Now go past it, nice and easy.
Shooting last, number known. My old coach called that a gift.
Final round. The others are done. Now it's you. Beat the number, sprout.
That's the number! It's yours!
Well, now. That'll win it.
Past the number! Go on, smile!
Three-point champion of Blossom Park! Put that name up by the fountain.
Champion! Back in my day, the prize was a free cone. Today, too. Rollie?
The best shooter in Blossom Park. Hollis wants a rematch, set shot only.
Ones at Blossom Park. First to eleven, make it take it. The bench is watching, so play clean.
One on one, the oldest game in the park. First to eleven. You score, you keep it.
Threes, folks. Three a side, first to twenty-one, ninety seconds on the clock. Share the ball like it's ice cream.
Now we've got a real run. Twenty-one wins, ninety-second clock. Back in my day, the clock was sundown.
Their ball. Dig in, sprout.
Check it up. Defense now.
Other side's ball. Stay in front.
Get low, youngster. Their ball.
Sunday bucket.
Pretty jumper.
That'll play.
Nice and easy.
Good. Real good.
Old-school. I like it.
From way back. Lovely.
Three! Rollie, ring it!
Deep one. Park felt that.
Ooh, from the petals!
That's a grown-up shot.
Soft. Like a petal.
Laid it in nice.
Old-timer finish. Beautiful.
Up and in.
Well, look at that!
Right through it!
Threw it down, sprout!
Petals everywhere!
Oh, the old tree shook!
Oh, now hold on. Hold everything!
Rollie dropped a cone on that!
Frame that one for the fountain!
Cornbread fell off the folding chair!
Right on top of them!
Forty years! Never! Never like that!
Bumped and still scored!
Bucket, and the whistle!
And a cherry on top!
Counts, plus the foul!
Not quite.
Rim wasn't having it.
Next time, sprout.
Close. Not close enough.
Airball. The bench noticed.
Missed everything. Even the petals.
Oh, Cornbread's going to talk.
My, my. Not even close.
Sent it back!
Rejected! Good hands, youngster!
Blocked! Rollie felt that!
Shooed it like a pigeon!
Oh, that's a Sunday block.
Nope! Not today!
Blocked. Humbling, isn't it?
Got stuffed. Happens.
Oh, that one got caught.
Try it again, sprout.
Stole it! Clean!
Took it right from them!
Ha! Didn't even see it!
Your ball now, sprout.
Quick hands, youngster!
Lost it. Hold on tighter.
Go on, fetch it.
Oh, they took your lunch.
Loose handle. Tighten it up.
Bring the defender a chair!
Crossed up! Petals flying!
Whoa, where'd the defender go?
Oh, that's just unkind!
The old-timers felt that!
Ha! Defender's at the fountain!
Fell for it!
Oldest trick in the park.
Fooled them. Patience pays.
Defender jumped at shadows!
Whistle. Hold up.
That's a call.
Easy now, play clean.
Rule book says no.
They answered. Answer back.
Other side scores. Your turn.
Well, they can play too.
Bucket for them. Stay patient.
Don't let that settle, sprout.
Oh, they meant that one.
That one's going in their scrapbook.
Easy, sprout. Get it back.
Loud one. Don't take it personal.
Unanswered, and the bench is counting.
Rolling now. Somebody stop this youngster.
Look at this run. Petals can't keep up.
That's a spring rain, folks. Steady, steady.
One more bucket, sprout. Then ice cream.
Their game point. One stop. Just one.
Game! Checkers table, you seeing this?
That's the game, sprout. The bench tips its caps.
Winner! Rollie, one cone, on the house!
Ballgame! Just like the old Sundays!
They take it. Run it back. I'm not going anywhere.
Other side wins it. Spring's long. Plenty more runs.
Game's theirs. The bench saw the effort, youngster. Come back.
Tied at the horn. Even the petals can't pick.
A tie. We'd have played till the lamps came on.
Beautiful pass!
Shared it. That's manners.
What a dime!
Found the open hooper.
Alley-oop! Oh, lovely!
Up top! Caught and flushed!
Lobbed it, they finished it!
Ten seconds, folks!
Clock's going. Ten left!
Hurry, sprout! Ten seconds!
Whole team's in bloom now!
Now that's a team!
All together now! Beautiful!
Game Night, folks! Four little events, points for every one, and a single champion takes home the bragging rights.
Welcome to Game Night. Back in my day, this was called Tuesday. Four events, points each, one champion.
Tonight's a little bit of everything, like Rollie's sundae. Four scoops, points on each, one champion.
Slam Rush. Twenty seconds, as many dunks as you can manage.
Strike Storm. Land hits on the pads. Quick now, quick.
Trick Gauntlet. Hop on a board and string some tricks together.
Hot Shot. Put shots on goal. The goal's the big thing, sprout.
Coin Storm. Grab every coin. First time this park's ever paid anybody.
Counters next. Patience. Let the jab come, then answer it.
And... go!
Off with you!
Begin, sprout!
Five seconds!
Hurry now, five left!
Last five, youngster!
That one's yours, sprout. Tuck those points away.
Event goes to you! Don't spend it all now.
Well done. The old-timers are nodding, and they never nod.
Won it! Knew you had that in you.
Rival takes that one. Plenty of night left.
Not yours, that one. Shake the petals off.
Lost that event. The next event doesn't know that.
A tie. Share the cone, you two.
Right down the middle. Nobody blinked.
Player two, your turn. Pass the controller gently.
Share nicely, now. Player two, you're up.
Game Night champion! Folks, that's the one they'll talk about on Sundays.
Champion of the whole night! The bench remembers, and so will Rollie.
Four events, and one youngster on top of them all. Make some noise, folks!
Rival takes the night. Close, though. Close enough to come right back.
Not your night, sprout. Best stories I know start with a loss.
